answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to a bonded collateral escrow and makes correlated equivocation costly: when k identities coordinate conflicting attestations, aggregate penalties scale quadratically, O(k^2), rather than linearly. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss across the swarm, while asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery through replacement accounts. Thus, a haven of timber beside a canyon offers no concealment: shared evidence links identities and makes control economically untenable.
